title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW dispute
evidence: Seth Wenig/AP hide caption toggle caption i Seth Wenig/AP SEOUL, South Korea — South Korea said Thursday it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine, stepping up its protest against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's recent revelation of a supposedly secret transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea. South Korea has accused Ukraine of violating a nondisclosure agreement on their transfer in mid-September, but Kyiv has denied agreeing to such a deal. South Korea's Foreign Ministry didn't say when the ambassador, Park Hee-chang, will be brought back home.

title: Russian strike on buses kills at least 30, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge
evidence: Russian strike on buses kills at least 30, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge. Another 18 people were wounded, said Donetsk regional head Vadym Filashkin, accusing Russia of targeting buses carrying passengers to kill as many civilians as possible. Moscow is yet to comment on the latest attack. Given the sharp deterioration of security in the two neighbouring cities, he said all public transport had been ordered to stop.

title: Medium-term borrowing costs for UK government hit 19-year high
evidence: The yield, or interest rate, on 10-year UK government bonds had jumped 0.06 percentage points by lunchtime in London, to 5.515%. Yields go up when bond prices go down. Yields on 20- and 30-year UK government bonds, which are known as gilts, had also risen significantly, to their highest level since as long ago as 1998. Recent dramatic moves in government bond markets have been driven by international factors, but will increase the pressure on John Healey ahead of his first budget as chancellor on 28 October.

title: Italy overhauls electoral system after fiercely contested debate
evidence: Lawmakers voted 227 to 164 in favour of moving to a fully proportional system, which Meloni has argued will boost the chance of clear winners and more stable government. A party or coalition which emerges with the largest share of the votes - provided this exceeds 42% - will be awarded 105 additional seats in parliament (70 in the lower house and 35 in the senate), which could turn a narrow victory into a more comfortable majority. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says the move will deliver more stable government, but opposition parties say her aim is to stay in power. Parties proposing to form a coalition will be required to put forward their joint candidate for prime minister, and their political programme, before any general election. title: Microsoft event debuts new AI-friendly hardware and Windows changes
evidence: In its first live event in two years, Microsoft today announced its newest Surface laptop, outlined a host of changes coming to Windows 11, and shared a vision of how local-AI and agentic workflows could reshape personal computing for those in the dev community as well as home enthusiasts. The device has a starting price of $2,599, and comes in various SoC and memory configurations, with either a 5120-core or 6144-core Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of LPDDR5x unified memory. It will begin shipping on October 16 and is available for pre-order now. While the new Ultra is clearly focused on the developer crowd, graphical performance was highlighted during the presentation to show off just how capable the laptop can be. By leaning on unified memory allocation rather than the physical VRAM limits of a traditional GPU, the laptop can assign its resources to handle modern gaming tasks as well as local AI development and deployment.

title: Asos says hacker accessed customers’ names, contact details and search histories
evidence: After carrying out a “detailed, 48-hour investigation” into the incident, Asos confirmed on Thursday that basic personal information had been accessed by an unidentified third party. Asos says hacker accessed customers’ names, contact details and search histories. Payment card details and passwords had not been accessed, the retailer added. Hackers gained access to a database of one of Asos’s third-party service providers by impersonating a “trusted contact” to gain access to one of its employee’s accounts, the retailer said. “The affected platforms were immediately locked down, ensuring that no further information could be accessed, and a full investigation was launched with the support of both internal and external cyber experts. However, the company warned: “Please remain cautious of unexpected messages or calls claiming to be from Asos.

title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds
evidence: On Wednesday evening the cyber criminals responsible contacted the BBC sharing a sample of the stolen data which showed the true extent of the hack. In its email to customers, Asos confirmed data profiles were taken but said no bank details or passwords were accessed. The UK fashion site explained to customers that hackers gained access to an Asos employee account by "impersonating a trusted contact to obtain log in credentials".

title: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain
evidence: "We did not want it to come to this," Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar wrote on social media, as he said 20 diplomats and the consul general would leave Israel while a task force of seven could remain in the building "with a very limited scope of activity". UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband responded that some staff had been "temporarily withdrawn" for security reasons, but stressed the mission will "work with the Palestinian people". Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain - BBC News BBC News Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain Image source, Reuters By Adam Goldsmith and James Landale , Diplomatic correspondent Published 8 October 2026, 07:35 BST Updated 5 hours ago Most diplomats will leave the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, Israel says, but the UK insists the building "will not be closing", and will operate as a "UK Mission". Israel said in September it would shut the consulate, in retaliation for UK sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank which are illegal under international law. It is distinct from the UK embassy in Tel Aviv, which is the UK's main diplomatic hub with Israel.

title: New electric car 'make or break for Jaguar'
evidence: The minimum cost of Jaguar's Type 01 is £130,000 in the UK and $130,500 in the US. title: Japan beer giants raided over suspicions they colluded to set the price of beverages
evidence: The commission’s secretary general, Hiroo Iwanari, confirmed an investigation had begun, but declined to give details. Officials from the Fair Trade Commission this week searched the offices of Asahi Breweries, Kirin Brewery, Suntory Beer and Sapporo Breweries – which together control more than 90% of the domestic market. Investigators probe Asahi, Kirin, Suntory and Sapporo breweries – which together control more than 90% of Japan’s beer market Japanese authorities have raided the country’s four biggest breweries over suspicions they colluded to set the price of beer and other beverages – a practice media reports said could have forced drinkers to pay over the odds. The companies said they would cooperate with authorities. Japanese media quoted sources as saying that sales managers and other executives from the breweries were suspected of meeting secretly over a prolonged period to coordinate on the timing and scale of retail price increases, which ranged from several yen to several dozen yen a time.
